title: Interpretation Clause - Definition of 'Document' and 'Evidence'
old_text: 'Document' means any matter expressed or described upon any substance by means of letters, figures or marks... 'Evidence' means and includes all statements which the Court permits or requires to be made before it by witnesses...
new_text: 'Document' includes electronic and digital records, emails, server logs, documents on computers, messages, website contents, location data, voice mails and messages stored on digital devices... 'Evidence' expressly includes electronic records produced for inspection.
punishment_old: General definitions of fact, document, evidence under 1872 framework.
punishment_new: Definitions comprehensively modernize 'document' and 'evidence' to include digital records, server logs, messages, and location data on par with paper.
explanation: BSA Section 2 modernizes the interpretation clause of IEA Section 3. Electronic and digital records are placed squarely on an equal statutory footing with physical paper documents.
source: Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (Act No. 47 of 2023), Section 2

title: How Much of Information Received from Accused May be Proved (Discovery Statement)
chapter: Relevancy of Facts - Admissions and Confessions
old_text: Provided that, when any fact is deposed to as discovered in consequence of information received from a person accused of any offence, in the custody of a police officer, so much of such information, whether it amounts to a confession or not, as relates distinctly to the fact thereby discovered, may be proved.
new_text: Provided that when any fact is deposed to as discovered in consequence of information received from a person accused of any offence, in the custody of a police officer, so much of such information, whether it amounts to a confession or not, as relates distinctly to the fact thereby discovered, may be proved.
punishment_old: Classic doctrine of confirmation by subsequent recovery.
punishment_new: Classic discovery rule codified as Section 23 of BSA.
explanation: The famed Section 27 of the Indian Evidence Act (admissibility of disclosure statements leading to recovery of weapons or articles) is now Section 23 of BSA.
source: Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (Act No. 47 of 2023), Section 23

title: Admissibility of Electronic Records
old_text: Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act, any information contained in an electronic record which is printed on a paper, stored, recorded or copied in optical or magnetic media... shall be deemed to be also a document... if conditions in sub-section (2) are satisfied...
new_text: Any information contained in an electronic record produced by a computer in the course of an activity regularly carried on, shall be deemed to be also a document... Accompanied by a certificate signed by the person in official custody or an expert, with schedule specifying device details.
punishment_old: Mandatory Section 65B certificate under Arjun Panditrao ruling.
punishment_new: Re-codified under Section 63 with streamlined certificate schedule in Annexure.
explanation: The ubiquitous Section 65B certificate for computer printouts, CDRs, CCTV footage, and WhatsApp chats is now Section 63 of BSA, accompanied by a prescribed statutory schedule.
source: Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (Act No. 47 of 2023), Section 63

title: Presumption as to Dowry Death
old_text: When the question is whether a person has committed the dowry death of a woman and it is shown that soon before her death such woman had been subjected by such person to cruelty or harassment for, or in connection with, any demand for dowry, the Court shall presume that such person had caused the dowry death.
new_text: When the question is whether a person has committed the dowry death of a woman and it is shown that soon before her death such woman had been subjected by such person to cruelty or harassment for, or in connection with, any demand for dowry, the Court shall presume that such person had caused the dowry death.
punishment_old: Mandatory reverse burden of proof ('shall presume').
punishment_new: Mandatory reverse burden of proof retained under Section 118 BSA.
explanation: The crucial reverse statutory presumption in dowry death cases ('shall presume') moved from IEA Section 113B to BSA Section 118, working in tandem with BNS Section 80.
source: Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (Act No. 47 of 2023), Section 118
